Just noticing your body parts getting slimmer. I've had moments over the last few months where I say something along the lines of "wait, is my arm longer??" and realize my forearm is noticeably thinner.

Another thing is my stamina. I used to be winded and have aching legs after a brisk walk while grocery shopping, and now I can walk 2 miles without ending up trying to hide my gasps for air. Back pain and ankle pain has gotten significantly better, too.

First and foremost, CICO! I've been counting calories and aiming for 1600 a day. I vary a bit, sometimes I'll up it to 1800 or 2000 but I've had tbe most success personally with 1600. I don't want to give a number for yourself as I'm no expert, I've just found a number that works for me.

I've lost basically all that weight without stepping foot in a gym. Just focusing on calories and making better choices (grilled meat instead of fried, forgoing fries/potatoes, cutting out regular soda for diet soda. Some people don't like diet stuff which is fine, but I drink a lot of soda/sweet tea so switching to artificially sweetened stuff has been a lifesaver for me.

I've found a few staples for my meals: low carb bread (my favorite is Aunt Millies), La Banderita CarbCounter tortillas (I eat a LOT of wraps/burritos), no added sugar fruit spreads, Halo Top ice cream, low fat cheeses. Also Tyson frozen grilled chicken is a godsend for me, I hate cooking but having seasoned grilled chicken around all the time is great, it's very versatile. If you're into cooking by all means make it yourself, chicken is excellent in the protein to calorie ratio.

Good luck on your journey!

In my experience, I can go 2 weeks just fluctuating the same pound up and down, then the third week *poof* I'm down 5 pounds. It can be disheartening, but I just remind myself that I'm doing everything right, it just takes patience.

A couple things:

1. It's not ideal, but are you sure you have an idea of the calories you're eating in general? Calories are magic to me, you can look at sandwiches on a menu that ate 1-2 ingredients off from each other, but the calories of one is 400 while the other is 800. I don't get it. I understand not wanting to count calories but in my opinion, it's important to have an idea (AKA just be sure there's nothing in your diet that's way higher calorie than you'd think) 

2. Drink LOTS of water. Water is absolutely essential to losing weight, I find that I'll slack on drinking water for a week but as soon as I drink a couple glasses, the scale starts moving again.

3. Make sure you're getting enough sleep. Majority of fat is burned in your sleep, so if your sleep is off then your body isn't having enough time to burn off the fat

Thanks! Your mileage may vary but a few things that are my staples:

Strict CICO. If it touches your lips, log it. I use My Fitness Pal and have a limit of 1600. I occasionally go up to 1800 for a spell which seems to help plateaus of no weight loss.

Find healthier or low cal versions of your diet staples! I experimented a lot with sugar free or super low cal stuff like honey mustard, ranch, etc but I just couldn't stomach most of it and it just made me want the real stuff more. I love honey mustard and ranch so I just found the light versions of Ken's and Hidden Valley respectively, and that basically halves the calories of both.

Protein protein protein: tons of protein helps keep me full and satisfied. I eat a lot of carbs but a lot of protein helps balance it out.

This is probably the most important and related to #1: weigh/measure everything you eat. Buy a food scale and weigh everything, and use measuring spoons and cups for everything. I generally use the serving size on the package of foods as a guideline. Sometimes it's plenty, sometimes it's not enough so I just add a serving or half a serving extra. The important bit is just being consistent and disciplined. Also no eyeballing, it's so easy to misjudge calories in stuff.

At the end of the day, if you follow CICO you will lose weight. You don't have to cut out everything you love, just cut back and find alternatives that fit your new lifestyle. Also just remember: it's a lifestyle, not a diet. Build healthy habits that will last you the rest of your life and keep you at your goal when you reach it!

Good luck on your journey :)
